bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to education finance; authorizing a grant for truancy crisis response; appropriating money.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1. APPROPRIATIONS.

Subdivision 1.

Department of Education.

The sums indicated in this section are appropriated from the general fund to the Department of Education in the fiscal years designated.

Subd. 2.

Truancy crisis response.

(a) For a grant to Hennepin County Community Action Partners:

$

1,500,000

.....

2026

$

1,500,000

.....

2027

(b) The grant recipient must use grant money to respond to the needs of children age eight to 18 years old involved with truancy in Hennepin County. The grant recipient must create culturally welcoming and nurturing spaces for interventions to stop truancy by addressing the needs of African American youth who are involved in truancy and the child protection system. Eligible uses of grant money for truancy crisis response include establishing mentoring relationships, re-engaging a child with their birth family or other relatives, preparing and assisting youth in finding meaningful work opportunities, and providing life skills training in trauma-informed practices and de-escalation skills.

(c) Any balance in fiscal year 2026 is available in fiscal year 2027.

(d) These are onetime appropriations.
additions: The sums indicated in this section are appropriated from the general fund to the Department of Education in the fiscal years designated.

(b) The grant recipient must use grant money to respond to the needs of children age eight to 18 years old involved with truancy in Hennepin County. The grant recipient must create culturally welcoming and nurturing spaces for interventions to stop truancy by addressing the needs of African American youth who are involved in truancy and the child protection system. Eligible uses of grant money for truancy crisis response include establishing mentoring relationships, re-engaging a child with their birth family or other relatives, preparing and assisting youth in finding meaningful work opportunities, and providing life skills training in trauma-informed practices and de-escalation skills.
(c) Any balance in fiscal year 2026 is available in fiscal year 2027.
